articles.title: From Alaskan bears to baby bats, these lives cams are a treat
articles.description: Ever wanted to watch bears catch salmon in Alaska or elephants gather around a watering hole in Africa? You might not get the chance to see these events in person, but thanks to a cool website called Explore.org Live Cams, you can watch them from your computer. The free website features more than 200 live cameras set up in wildlife locations around the world. You can watch brown bears fishing at Brooks Falls in Alaska, check out the infamous Trempealeau Eagles in their nest, or get spooked by the eyeshine of Nile crocodiles on the Mara Fig Tree crossing night cam. The site also has live feeds of rescue kittens, puppies, and other animals living in shelters and care centers. I’m a big fan of the Mixed Species Flying Fox cam, which is set up at the Lubee Bat Conservancy in Gainesville. There’s just something about watching furry bats munching on fruit all day that warms the heart. Many of the cameras also include interesting facts about the animals, local weather information, and comment sections where you can chat with other people watching. There’s even a collection of snapshots so you can see what you might’ve missed. There’s no guarantee anything exciting will happen and you might spend half an hour staring at an empty riverbank. But that makes it all the more exciting when you do witness something. Just like the wildly popular Dutch Fish Doorbell, these live cams give you something relaxing to have on in the background while you work and help us connect with nature just a tad bit more, even in the confines of our cubicles. For more fun and helpful tips, tricks, website and app recommendations, be sure to subscribe to our PCWorld Try This newsletter.

articles.title: Sheriffs Say Greg Abbott Is Lying About Their Endorsements
articles.description: Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott publicized the endorsements of 11 Democratic sheriffs. Three of them denied ever endorsing him. Zapata County Sheriff Ramon Montes, Val Verde County Sheriff Joe Frank Martinez, and Webb County Sheriff Marin Cuellar all publicly announced that they were not endorsing Abbot after he posted them on his endorsement list on Monday. While Cuellar has been removed from the list, Montes and Martinez are still on it. “Please remove my name from this for the Governor Abbott. This is Sheriff Martin Cuellar. The governor endorsed Tano my brother’s opponent,” Cuellar wrote in a text screenshot he posted on Facebook. Cuellar is the brother of Democratic Representative Henry Cuellar, who is currently running for Texas’s 28th House district. “I want to make it unequivocally clear that I have not issued a political endorsement of Governor Greg Abbott, and I did not authorize anyone to use my name as an endorsement,” Martinez wrote in his own official statement. “I made it clear to the Sheriff who submitted the endorsement that I could not endorse Governor Abbott. I also made it clear that no one from the Governor’s office ever contacted me regarding an endorsement, and that I do not need anyone speaking on my behalf.” Sheriff Montes’s office told Border Report that he “is not endorsing anyone at this time.” Recent polling has Abbott sitting just three points ahead of his Democratic challenger, former state Representative Gina Hinosoja.

articles.title: Feds Arrest Top Democratic Leader in Redistricting Fight
articles.description: Virginia Senate President L. Louise Lucas, the Democratic leader behind the state’s redistricting effort, was arrested Thursday in connection with an alleged bribery and racketeering scheme. In a 45-page indictment filed in the Eastern District of Virginia, Lucas and six co-defendants were charged with conspiring to distribute and possess marijuana, conspiring to launder money, laundering money, and committing bribery by distributing large quantities of illegal marijuana under the auspices of her legal medical cannabis business. Lucas, an 82-year-old great-grandmother, has served in the Virginia Senate since 1992. She faces five of the eight charges included in the indictment. These charges arrive five months after the FBI raided Lucas’s office in Portsmouth, Virginia, and the neighboring cannabis dispensary she co-owns. In a phone call in February 2026, Lucas discussed the language surrounding the state’s pending recreational marijuana legislation with an unindicted co-conspirator, according to the charging document. During the phone call, Lucas spoke about the possibility of the co-conspirator receiving a license, and sharing the proceeds with her because “this is our last chance at generational wealth.” “I’ve got too old to not be greedy,” Lucas said, according to the indictment. In another phone call a month later, Lucas said she hoped that the cannabis legislation would pass in order to make what she’d done legal, because “when I did it, it was obviously illegal.” Lucas has been a frequent critic of Republicans and President Donald Trump, and is an ally to Virginia’s Democratic Governor Abigail Spanberger. The state senator was a central figure in mounting her party’s redistricting efforts earlier this year, which were ultimately blocked by the Virginia Supreme Court. This story has been updated.

articles.title: Trump Boots Two Outlets From Press Pool Despite Renewed Legal Threats
articles.description: The president is tacking on to his White House media ban. The White House stripped media access from CNN and The Independent’s Andrew Feinberg on Wednesday, despite the fact that both were scheduled to provide pool coverage. “Today is CNN’s turn to fulfill both in-town and out-of-town TV pool duties, but the White House press office left the network off the list for Donald Trump’s trip to South Carolina, so as a result there will be no pooled TV coverage of the trip,” wrote CNN’s chief media analyst, Brian Stelter, on X. CNN attorney Ted Boutrous had warned the Justice Department earlier this week that the network would take legal action if the White House continued to exclude CNN from Air Force One. Boutrous is also representing MS NOW and Politico, which faced the initial wave of Trump’s restrictions alongside CNN last month. He noted in a letter that the White House had until 5 p.m. on Thursday to respond to the developing situation with CNN, or the organization “will be forced to pursue additional judicial relief.” Semafor’s Maxwell Tani confirmed that Feinberg was also on the outs, sharing on X that “without explanation, the White House told him today that he would no longer be the print pooler on Trump’s Thursday trip.” The decision came just two days after Trump tore into Feinberg during a White House presser, shushing and demeaning the well-reputed journalist. “I don’t know who the hell you are, but you better be careful,” Trump said on Tuesday, minutes after Feinberg had introduced himself. Moments later, Trump called Feinberg a “sick person” and added, “I actually think there’s something wrong with you.” The president’s official rapid response account on X added fuel to the fire later that day, recirculating the exchange with a new description for Feinberg: “Mongoloid Moron.”
